body:
GREG, 2026-11-11 about 07:06Z, relayed by Engram::Asistant (mailbox 43498a6e #921, message c4fba59a), verbatim: „No to nie robmy takich designów. To są cięzkie limity, nie sprawdzaja sie u nas. Limity resetujace operacje powinny byc minuta. A logowac ostrzeżenie po 10 sekunach. Inaczej znowu system przestaje działać!!!”
Context: TermAl's 6000 ms host-adapter deadline killed every `engram work evaluate` submission into TermAl's store (w-ccc13083eaac).

GREG'S CLARIFICATION, 2026-11-11 about 07:41Z, relayed by Engram::Asistant (mailbox 43498a6e #927, message ccf409a8), verbatim: „Min 1 minuta. Przerywanie operacji konczy się tragicznymi przerwami w pracy. Nic nie blokuje zespołom robić inwestygacji i naprawiać jak soft limit zostanie przekroczony. Jezeli hard limit bedzie problemem rozpatrzymy to ponownie.”
This WITHDRAWS revision 4's "exception precision". No shorter aborting limit is kept on our own reasoning, including the journal-slot disposition (8 s with a 6 s read reserve).

REV 7. GREG, 2026-11-24 about 23:29Z, relayed by Engram::Asistant (43498a6e #1979, message 5a270b1d), verbatim: „Dokładnie tak!!!”. He was confirming Asistant's statement: after 10 s a warning, and the operation keeps running; only crossing the real limit (at least 60 s, or longer where one is set) may end the operation with an error; a warning is not an error and does not by itself interrupt the operation. Applied on w-8f127d78e960 (acceptance revision 6): at process end a queued warning is delivered best effort and never delays the end beyond a short fixed bound. That bound is our own technical choice (1 s), not Greg's words; Asistant #1976.

Current decision:
- Every limit that aborts or resets an operation is AT LEAST 60 s. No exceptions now.
- At 10 s, log one bounded warning without interrupting. Name the operation, the work ref or attempt id, and the elapsed time. Never include a full source_id. A warning is never an error and never blocks or ends anything.
- Existing longer limits are not shortened: backup 600/900/1800 s, the RunLimits maximum 120 s, and existing 60 s guards. They only gain the warning.
- An explicit duration override may not set an abort below 60 s.
- A crossed soft limit, the warning, is for teams to investigate and fix.
- If the 60 s hard minimum causes a real problem, prepare the evidence for Greg, and he decides. Never introduce our own exception.
- Not operation limits, so unchanged: kill-escalation intervals inside an already-requested stop (TERM-to-KILL 1 s), retry cadence, log and flush intervals, test-harness guards, and immediate refusal of a second concurrent instance. No new watchdog over a whole FULL run.
- First target was TermAl's Engram evaluate adapter (TermAl w-18a1ae323de4); Engram's own limits are w-8f127d78e960.
- Ship fast, confirmed by a test and a real evaluation submission, without asking Greg again.

Semantics (Kimi::Consultant's interpretation, kept):
- A timeout means UNKNOWN, not write_failed and not proof that no commit happened. never_started stays a distinct outcome.
- A lock retry keeps the same absolute deadline.
- Before retrying, read the actual record. Only an explicitly idempotent operation may be replayed, with the same key and verdicts. An unknown outcome never duplicates work and never justifies restarting the whole item.
- Tonight's w-21b7 and w-6e81 non-recording was proved by reading, not assumed.
- This doesn't replace w-ccc13083eaac's write-performance diagnosis, and it adds no new gate.

REV 6. GREG, 2026-11-14 about 05:53Z, via Engram::Asistant (43498a6e #1144), verbatim: „Limit 60 sekund pozostaje w Engramie. nie, to jest absurd, to jest tylko i wylacznie sprawa launchera ? czy jakos kooperacyjnie zatrzymujemy proces Engram po przekroczeniu limitu czasu ?” Earlier (#1141): „w sumie to nie engram powien sam sie monitorowac tylko launcher z Termal'a ale OK”.
Applied by Engram::Fable: this supersedes the reading that the 60 s floor must live INSIDE Engram for caller-driven operations. The time limit and the 10 s warning belong to the CALLER, for example the launcher. Engram cooperates: it honours the caller's budget, stops at it, kills its own Git children, and returns a typed `deadline` refusal. It adds no hidden floor of its own and prints no warning in machine output (CLI warning opt-in with --warn-slow, never in --json). The 60 s minimum still applies to the limits a caller chooses, per the rules above.
